changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For product and engineering buyers: "Stop billing being a tax on your roadmap. Change a price and ship a new tier in minutes, not a quarter." Lead with roadmap time returned to engineers, not revenue growth.
changes.why: Owen rejected the revenue framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap') and the demo only landed when it was translated into roadmap time ('a quarter of roadmap in five minutes').

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance-gated deals: "Put a number on the cost of not fixing it. We build your payback case with you, using your own figures, before any budget review." Offer a customer-specific value session as the first response when a champion asks for payback, and keep the generic study as a supporting proof point only.
changes.why: Owen asked for 'something that shows payback' and said he couldn't get past the CFO 'without a number that's ours', and we sent only the general ROI deck; the planned session to build their own number never happened.

changes.change: For buyers worried about switching off a homegrown billing system: a staged migration story (move in stages, no re-collecting cards), backed by a named customer reference who has done it. Lead with this instead of a migration doc. Note that the customer said 'we don't touch billing before renewal season', so show how the staging works around that timing.
changes.why: Migration was the runner-up loss reason, and the customer wanted a peer who had done it but received a doc; whether a reference was ever offered is unknown, so this is a hypothesis to test.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For billing buyers with finance in the loop, add a revenue-leak proof point: "Some subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it. Quantify that leak in your value case, so finance sees a cost of doing nothing." Use it as a hook in the customer-specific payback case, not as a standalone feature line.
changes.why: Owen mentioned lapsed subscriptions from failed cards once and nobody added it up, though it is the kind of concrete cost finance responds to.
